title: Module-derived global cohomology is the cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the common coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention] and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. For a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] write $F_{ab}$ for its underlying abelian sheaf and $\Gamma(\mathcal C,F)$ for the group of compatible families of sections $(s_U)_{U\in\mathcal C}$ [def-sfb-coefficient-module-global-sections]; no final object of $\mathcal C$ is assumed. Let $R\Gamma(\mathcal C,-):D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathrm{Ab})$ be the unbounded right derived functor of $\Gamma(\mathcal C,-)$ on $\mathcal O$-modules, computed on K-injective complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], and let $H^n(\mathcal C,F_{ab})$ be the $n$th right derived functor of $\Gamma(\mathcal C,-)$ on abelian sheaves, computed by injective resolutions in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then for every integer $n\geq0$ there is a canonical additive isomorphism $$H^n\bigl(R\Gamma(\mathcal C,F[0])\bigr)\cong H^n(\mathcal C,F_{ab}),$$ natural in $F$, which in degree $0$ is the identity of $\Gamma(\mathcal C,F)$. In particular it is $\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$-linear, where $a\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ acts on both sides through the module endomorphism of $F$ given by multiplication by $a$. No flatness of $\mathcal O$ over the constant sheaf $\mathbf Z$ and no injectivity of $F_{ab}$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $Z=\underline{\mathbf Z}_{\mathcal C}$. Abelian sheaves are exactly $Z$-module sheaves: for an abelian sheaf $A$, give a locally constant integer section $z$ its action by choosing a covering on which $z$ is represented by integers $n_i$, and glue the sections $n_i a|_{U_i}$. Local representability and local equality are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], applied to the constant integer presheaf of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. On a common refinement the two choices give the same integer multiples, so the sheaf axiom makes this action well defined. The module laws and compatibility with restriction hold on those coverings and hence globally. Conversely any unital $Z$-action must act on integer sections by repeated addition, and then on all sections by this local formula. Every additive sheaf map respects the formula. Thus this construction and forgetting are inverse additive equivalences, preserving the underlying section families and every map. Kernels and cokernels are preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions]. The unique maps from $\mathbf Z$ to $\mathcal O(U)$ induce the sheaf ring map $Z\to\mathcal O$; restriction along it is precisely this integer action on $F_{ab}$.

source.place: Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification; elementary integer-action construction using the sheaf axiom

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-derived-sections-scalar-coherence] with $R=Z$, $S=\mathcal O$, the map just constructed, and the complex $F[0]$. Its hypotheses are exactly a small site and commutative ring sheaves in the common coefficient universe; its global sections are $\operatorname{Hom}(1,M_{ab})$, the compatible families in [def-sfb-coefficient-module-global-sections], even when the site has no final object. It gives the natural isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ $$\sigma_F:R\Gamma_{\mathcal O}(F[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_Z(F_{ab}[0]).$$ This is the coefficient-restriction comparison fixed by the derived-unit equation in the cited statement, so it is the canonical comparison, rather than a choice of an abstract isomorphism. In particular its construction requires neither flatness nor preservation of injectives by forgetting $\mathcal O$-modules.

proof.text: Choose an abelian injective resolution $F_{ab}[0]\to J^\bullet$, zero in negative degrees; existence follows from [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives] and the injective-resolution construction of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The equivalence of step 1 carries this to a $Z$-module injective resolution by [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions]. It is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so the definition [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] computes $R\Gamma_Z(F_{ab}[0])$ by $\Gamma(\mathcal C,J^\bullet)$. On the other hand this very complex computes the right-derived abelian-sheaf cohomology in the statement. Consequently $$H^n(R\Gamma_Z(F_{ab}[0]))=H^n(\Gamma(\mathcal C,J^\bullet))\cong H^n(\mathcal C,F_{ab}).$$ The resolution identifications are canonical and natural: a morphism of abelian sheaves lifts to a map of their injective resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists], and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] computes its induced maps by this same sectionwise chain map. Thus both descriptions give identical maps.

Take $H^n$ of $\sigma_F$ and follow it by step 3. This gives the requested additive isomorphism and its naturality. In degree zero the augmentation identifies the kernel of $\Gamma(J^0)\to\Gamma(J^1)$ with $\Gamma(F_{ab})$, since compatible-family sections preserve kernels. The derived-unit equation defining $\sigma_F$ in [lem-coef-derived-sections-scalar-coherence] identifies this augmentation with the identical underived section family; hence the comparison is the identity on $\Gamma(\mathcal C,F)$. Finally, for $a\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, multiplication $m_a:F\to F$ is a module map because $\mathcal O$ is commutative. Naturality for $m_a$ says explicitly $c_F H^n(R\Gamma(m_a))=H^n(\mathcal C,(m_a)_{ab})c_F$, which is the asserted scalar linearity.
